briefing:
The Orrin Eastside clinic is scheduled to see its first patient appointments on Tuesday 29 June 2027. This briefing pulls together the latest status updates and emails on the opening, starting with ownership of the main workstreams. Joaquin Kowalczyk owns the building fit-out, Lucía Oyelaran owns equipment procurement, Zainab Takahashi owns clinical staffing, Yuki Valdés owns patient records, and Elif Kaur owns regulatory approval. A rise in insurance premiums could affect the number of treatment chairs.

On the building side, the fit-out is scheduled to end on Wednesday 24 February 2027. Working days are Monday to Friday, and there are no public holidays in this period. The pharmacy stock delivery is on Monday 12 April 2027, and it appears in the plan alongside the other physical preparations for the site.

Equipment installation can begin 8 working days after the building fit-out ends. That rule is the one the equipment procurement workstream is working to, and it is stated here as written in the source updates rather than converted into a calendar date. The imaging equipment lease is worth €66,500. Late delivery of the X-ray unit could delay the first day of patient appointments. All sign-offs, handovers, deliveries and meetings in this note take place on working days.

On capacity, the plan provides for 32 treatment chairs. An additional 3 treatment chairs were approved in March. The updates received do not state a combined chair figure, so none is given here. Unfilled nurse vacancies could delay the first day of patient appointments.

The budget position also changed in March. The approved project budget is €541,000, and the steering group approved a reduction of €23,000 to the project budget in March. The updates do not state a revised budget figure, so the two amounts are reported separately as they were given. The figure of €541,000 is the budget as first approved, before the changes listed in this note.

Looking ahead to the weeks before opening, the staff induction day is on Thursday 1 July 2027, and the open evening for residents is on Thursday 8 July 2027. Both dates are included in the schedule as supplied. Further updates from the workstream owners will be added to this briefing as they arrive. Higher energy tariffs could affect the budget.

briefing:
The Brightwater classroom technology refresh has an approved project budget of £387,000. In March the steering group approved a reduction of £46,000 to the project budget. The device leasing agreement is worth £20,500. Each of these figures comes from the latest status updates and is quoted as written there. Rising support fees could affect the budget. The figure of £387,000 is the budget as first approved, before the changes listed in this note.

On equipment, the plan provides for 132 laptops, and an additional 23 laptops were approved in March. Teodor Szabo owns the asset tagging workstream, so questions about labelling and inventory records go through him. Leilani Demir owns the safeguarding filters workstream, which links to the safeguarding review on Tuesday 25 May 2027.

Thandiwe Kaur owns the network upgrade workstream. The network upgrade is scheduled to end on Thursday 24 June 2027. Working days are Monday to Friday, and there are no public holidays in this period. A shortage of charging trolleys could delay the first lessons on the new devices.

Device deployment can begin 4 working days after the network upgrade ends. That rule is the one recorded in the plan, and the updates do not add anything further to it. The first lessons on the new devices are planned for Tuesday 3 August 2027. Higher insurance costs could affect the number of laptops. All sign-offs, handovers, deliveries and meetings in this note take place on working days.

Idris Mensah owns the teacher training workstream, and Freya Kowalczyk owns the parent communications workstream. Both of these sit alongside the technical work and feed into the first lessons on the new devices. Delays in the wireless survey could delay the first lessons on the new devices.

Several fixed dates are already in the diary. The supplier demo is on Wednesday 21 April 2027, and the safeguarding review follows on Tuesday 25 May 2027. The governors' meeting is on Thursday 23 September 2027, which comes after the first lessons planned for Tuesday 3 August 2027.

This note brings together what the status updates and emails currently say, and it will be revised as further updates arrive from the workstream owners.

briefing:
The Bramblecote office relocation is progressing across several workstreams, and this briefing pulls together the latest status updates and emails. The approved project budget is £257,000. In March the steering group approved an increase of £35,000 to the project budget, and the same month saw approval of an additional 23 desks on top of the 144 desks the plan provides for. Higher-than-expected furniture prices could affect the number of desks. The figure of £257,000 is the budget as first approved, before the changes listed in this note.

On ownership, Freya Kowalczyk owns the lease negotiation workstream, while Mei Mensah owns the furniture procurement workstream. The furniture supplier contract is worth £44,500, and the furniture delivery is on Thursday 25 February 2027. Marisol Okafor owns the moving logistics workstream, which will be closely tied to the timing of the staff move-in.

The network cabling installation is scheduled to end on Monday 22 March 2027. Ingrid Demir owns the security badges workstream, and the security audit is on Thursday 1 April 2027. Sanna Iyer owns the staff communications workstream and is responsible for sharing the relevant dates with staff as they are confirmed. Rising removal costs could affect the budget.

The staff move-in can begin 5 working days after the network cabling installation ends. Working days are Monday to Friday, and there are no public holidays in this period. The move-in rule is stated in those terms in the source updates, so it is reproduced here as written. A dispute over the lift installation could delay the official opening of the new office. All sign-offs, handovers, deliveries and meetings in this note take place on working days.

Looking further ahead, the official opening of the new office is planned for Wednesday 7 July 2027. The landlord walkthrough is on Thursday 21 October 2027. Both entries are recorded in the project calendar alongside the earlier milestones, and the workstream owners named above continue to supply updates for their own areas as the relocation moves forward. A delay in fire-safety certification could delay the official opening of the new office.

briefing:
The Silvercap classroom technology refresh is progressing through its planning stages, and this note pulls together the latest from status updates and emails. The approved project budget is £216,000, and the device leasing agreement is worth £42,500. In March the steering group approved a reduction of £40,000 to the project budget, and the same month saw approval of an additional 8 laptops. The plan provides for 544 laptops. Late approval of the content filter could delay the first lessons on the new devices. The figure of £216,000 is the budget as first approved, before the changes listed in this note.

Ownership of the workstreams is now settled. Idris Mwangi owns the device procurement workstream, while Tomasz Raman owns asset tagging. Corentin Sørensen owns the safeguarding filters workstream, and Marisol Takahashi owns parent communications. Oluwaseun Kowalczyk owns teacher training. Device breakage rates could affect the budget.

On the network side, the upgrade is scheduled to end on Friday 14 May 2027. That date matters for everything that follows in the schedule, since the wider rollout is sequenced behind it.

Device deployment can begin 3 working days after the network upgrade ends. Working days are Monday to Friday, and there are no public holidays in this period. The first lessons on the new devices are planned for Wednesday 2 June 2027. A shortage of charging trolleys could delay the first lessons on the new devices. All sign-offs, handovers, deliveries and meetings in this note take place on working days.

Several fixed events sit around the rollout. The safeguarding review is on Tuesday 16 March 2027, which falls within the safeguarding filters workstream led by Corentin Sørensen. The parents' evening is on Tuesday 25 May 2027, and Marisol Takahashi's parent communications work connects directly to it. The teacher training day is on Thursday 18 November 2027, and Oluwaseun Kowalczyk holds that workstream.

Taken together, the budget decisions, the laptop numbers, the workstream owners and the calendar of events give a consistent picture of where the refresh currently stands, based on the updates received so far. Higher insurance costs could affect the number of laptops.

briefing:
The approved project budget for the Brightwater annual partner conference is £303,000, and the conference opening day is planned for Tuesday 23 November 2027. The plan provides for 750 delegate places. In March, the steering group approved a reduction of £10,000 to the project budget, and an additional 120 delegate places were approved in the same month. A clash with a rail strike could delay the conference opening day. The figure of £303,000 is the budget as first approved, before the changes listed in this note.

Ownership of the workstreams is divided as follows. Ingrid Mwangi owns the venue booking workstream, and Yuki Quiroga owns the registration workstream. Leilani Raman owns the speaker programme workstream, while Marisol Castellanos owns the catering workstream. Bastian Sørensen owns the audio-visual production workstream, which includes the audio-visual production contract worth £50,500.

On the venue side, venue contract signature is scheduled to end on Friday 18 June 2027. The sponsor call is on Wednesday 9 June 2027, so it falls ahead of that signature end date in the calendar. Low early registrations could affect the budget.

Ticket sales can begin 5 working days after venue contract signature ends. For this purpose, working days are Monday to Friday, and there are no public holidays in this period. That rule is the one the registration workstream will be working from when it plans its opening of sales. A sponsor withdrawing could affect the number of delegate places. All sign-offs, handovers, deliveries and meetings in this note take place on working days.

Two preparation sessions are also in the diary. The registration desk training is on Monday 22 February 2027, and the dress rehearsal is on Wednesday 17 March 2027. Both sit with the wider delivery plan for the conference, alongside the budget and delegate place decisions taken in March. The keynote speaker's visa delay could delay the conference opening day.

This briefing has been compiled from the latest status updates and emails from the workstream owners. Any further changes to the figures or dates above will be recorded in later updates as they are confirmed by the steering group and the individual workstream owners.

briefing:
The Pellucid flagship store launch is now being tracked through five workstreams, each with a named owner. Leilani Bakshi owns the shop fit-out, Corentin Brennan owns stock buying, Teodor Nakamura owns the marketing campaign, Lucía Takahashi owns staff recruitment, and Elif Okafor owns security. This note pulls together the latest status updates and emails so the picture sits in one place. Weaker footfall forecasts could affect the number of staff hires.

On budget, the approved project budget is €102,000. The steering group approved a reduction of €57,000 to the project budget in March. The shop-fitting contract is worth €17,500, and it forms part of the fit-out workstream that Leilani Bakshi leads. The figure of €102,000 is the budget as first approved, before the changes listed in this note.

The shop fit-out is scheduled to end on Friday 28 May 2027. For planning purposes, the team is working to a Monday to Friday working week, and there are no public holidays in this period. That working-week basis matters for the stock side of the plan, since the stock loading rule is expressed in working days. All sign-offs, handovers, deliveries and meetings in this note take place on working days.

Stock loading can begin 3 working days after the shop fit-out ends. Corentin Brennan's stock buying workstream is the one that will pick up from that point. Earlier in the calendar, the stock count is on Friday 5 February 2027, which sits well ahead of the fit-out and loading period. A delay in the signage permit could delay the store opening.

Recruitment is progressing under Lucía Takahashi. The plan provides for 34 staff hires, and an additional 4 staff hires were approved in March. Both figures are recorded as stated in the approvals, and this note does not combine them. Late delivery of the till system could delay the store opening.

Looking at the later milestones, the marketing review is on Wednesday 21 July 2027, and Teodor Nakamura's campaign workstream is the one that feeds into it. The store opening is planned for Wednesday 8 September 2027. The fire-safety inspection is on Wednesday 22 September 2027, and Elif Okafor's security workstream is listed alongside these closing milestones in the latest updates. Higher rent from the service charge could affect the budget.

briefing:
The Ashgrove CRM migration is being coordinated across several workstreams, and this briefing pulls together the latest information from status updates and emails. The go-live of the new CRM is planned for Tuesday 16 November 2027. The approved project budget is $97,000, and the vendor implementation contract is worth $83,500. Low dashboard adoption could affect the number of user licences. The figure of $97,000 is the budget as first approved, before the changes listed in this note.

On ownership, Zainab Sørensen owns the data cleansing workstream, while Freya Marchetti owns the vendor management workstream. Sanna Oyelaran owns the reporting dashboards workstream. Mei Haddad owns the access control workstream, and Priya Achterberg owns the user training workstream.

Several milestones have been scheduled. The security review is on Friday 19 February 2027, and the steering committee meeting is on Wednesday 31 March 2027. The data migration is scheduled to end on Thursday 3 June 2027. The data-quality checkpoint is on Wednesday 8 September 2027. Incomplete customer data mappings could delay the go-live of the new CRM.

Decisions taken in March also affect the project's shape. The steering group approved an increase of $34,000 to the project budget in March. In the same month, an additional 16 user licences were approved, and the plan provides for 167 user licences. Licence price increases could affect the budget.

On testing, user acceptance testing can begin 5 working days after the data migration ends. For this purpose, working days are Monday to Friday, and there are no public holidays in this period. The sequence of the migration, the checkpoint and the go-live is therefore laid out in the schedule, with the individual workstream owners responsible for their respective areas of delivery. A delay in single sign-on setup could delay the go-live of the new CRM. All sign-offs, handovers, deliveries and meetings in this note take place on working days.

Further detail on each workstream can be drawn from the status updates held by the owners named above, and the figures and dates in this briefing are reproduced as they appear in the source material.

On ownership, Tomasz Mwangi owns the shop fit-out workstream, and Marisol Abernethy owns the stock buying workstream. Anders Raman owns the marketing campaign workstream, while Amara Haddad owns the security workstream. Zainab Okafor owns the staff recruitment workstream, which is working to a plan that provides for 61 staff hires. In March, an additional 3 staff hires were approved.

On budget, the approved project budget is €236,000. In March the steering group approved an increase of €49,000 to the project budget. Separately, the shop-fitting contract is worth €37,000. The figures are reported here as they appear in the updates. A shortfall in seasonal stock could delay the store opening. The figure of €236,000 is the budget as first approved, before the changes listed in this note.

The shop fit-out is scheduled to end on Wednesday 17 March 2027. Once the fit-out has finished, the schedule for the next stage is set by a simple rule: working days are Monday to Friday, and there are no public holidays in this period. Weaker footfall forecasts could affect the number of staff hires. All sign-offs, handovers, deliveries and meetings in this note take place on working days.

Stock loading can begin 8 working days after the shop fit-out ends. Stock buying, under Marisol Abernethy, feeds directly into that stage, so the two workstreams will be closely linked as the date approaches. Rising wage costs could affect the budget.

Several reviews and events are already scheduled in the run-up to opening. The marketing review is on Friday 30 April 2027, and the fire-safety inspection is on Friday 21 May 2027. The press preview follows on Friday 2 July 2027, ahead of the store opening on Friday 29 October 2027. Late delivery of the till system could delay the store opening.

Further updates will be added to this briefing as the workstream owners report in, and the milestones above remain the reference points for the programme as it currently stands.

briefing:
The Dunmore CRM migration has an approved project budget of $215,000, and the vendor implementation contract is worth $63,500. The go-live of the new CRM is planned for Wednesday 16 June 2027. The data migration is scheduled to end on Monday 22 February 2027, and the steering committee meets on Wednesday 17 March 2027 to review progress. The figure of $215,000 is the budget as first approved, before the changes listed in this note.

Ownership of the workstreams is divided among five colleagues. Freya Castellanos owns the vendor management workstream, and Emeka Brennan owns the data cleansing workstream. Joaquin Takahashi owns user training, while Hamid Abernethy owns access control. Mei Nakamura owns the reporting dashboards workstream. Low dashboard adoption could affect the budget.

On the licensing side, the plan provides for 276 user licences. In March, an additional 52 user licences were approved. The steering group also approved a reduction of $59,000 to the project budget in March. These items are recorded as separate approvals, and this briefing reports them as they appear in the status updates. Incomplete customer data mappings could delay the go-live of the new CRM.

Several dates sit between now and go-live. The vendor demo is on Monday 26 April 2027, and the data-quality checkpoint is on Friday 13 August 2027. Both are recorded in the project calendar alongside the go-live date.

On testing, user acceptance testing can begin 10 working days after the data migration ends. Working days are Monday to Friday, and there are no public holidays in this period. The briefing leaves the arithmetic of that rule to the project plan and does not restate a start date here. Late fixes from the vendor could delay the go-live of the new CRM. All sign-offs, handovers, deliveries and meetings in this note take place on working days.

Further updates will be compiled from the workstream owners and from the outcomes of the steering committee meeting, and will be circulated in the same format as this briefing once the material has been gathered. Overtime costs for the support team could affect the number of user licences.

briefing:
The Bramblecote CRM migration has a planned go-live of Wednesday 6 October 2027 for the new CRM. The approved project budget is $204,000, which includes an increase of $39,000 that the steering group approved in March. The vendor implementation contract is worth $68,500, and the plan provides for 242 user licences. An additional 20 user licences were approved in March as well. Licence price increases could affect the budget. The figure of $204,000 is the budget as first approved, before the changes listed in this note.

Workstream ownership has been settled across the team. Bastian Castellanos owns the data cleansing workstream, while Kwame Bakshi owns the vendor management workstream. Idris Delacroix owns the access control workstream, and Rafael Oyelaran owns the integration testing workstream. Marisol Raman owns the reporting dashboards workstream. A delay in single sign-on setup could delay the go-live of the new CRM.

On the data side, the data migration is scheduled to end on Friday 12 March 2027. The planning convention is that working days are Monday to Friday, and there are no public holidays in this period. That convention matters for the testing schedule, since the data migration schedule feeds directly into the start of later activities. Low dashboard adoption could affect the number of user licences. All sign-offs, handovers, deliveries and meetings in this note take place on working days.

User acceptance testing can begin 3 working days after the data migration ends. Rafael Oyelaran's integration testing workstream sits alongside that testing phase, and the team will be working from the same schedule while both proceed.

Several fixed events are already in the calendar. The trainer briefing is on Thursday 8 April 2027, and the security review is on Thursday 29 July 2027. The vendor demo is on Thursday 4 November 2027. Kwame Bakshi, as owner of vendor management, is the contact for the vendor-facing items.

This briefing has been compiled from the latest status updates and emails circulating within the project team. Further detail on each workstream will be added by the respective owners as their plans are confirmed. Late fixes from the vendor could delay the go-live of the new CRM.

briefing:
The Ostrava classroom technology refresh is being run through five workstreams, and this note pulls together the latest position from the status updates and emails. Marisol Sørensen owns the network upgrade workstream, which is scheduled to end on Friday 23 April 2027. Hamid Nakamura owns device procurement, and Lucía Kaur owns teacher training.

On the device side, the plan provides for 495 laptops. In March, an additional 57 laptops were approved, and the figures are reported here as they were given in the updates, without being combined. The device leasing agreement is worth £74,500, and it sits within the procurement workstream that Hamid is managing. Device breakage rates could affect the number of laptops.

Timing for deployment is tied directly to the network work. Device deployment can begin 3 working days after the network upgrade ends. For this purpose, working days are Monday to Friday, and there are no public holidays in this period. The first lessons on the new devices is planned for Thursday 11 November 2027, which is the point at which the teaching side of the programme becomes visible to pupils. All sign-offs, handovers, deliveries and meetings in this note take place on working days.

On finances, the approved project budget is £507,000. The steering group also approved a reduction of £52,000 to the project budget in March. Both figures appear in the latest financial update, and they are recorded here as separate items exactly as stated by the group. Higher insurance costs could affect the budget. The figure of £507,000 is the budget as first approved, before the changes listed in this note.

Several fixed events shape the communications and assurance calendar. The parents' evening is on Friday 26 March 2027, and Joaquin Novak owns the parent communications workstream that covers it. The governors' meeting is on Wednesday 21 July 2027. The safeguarding review is on Thursday 30 September 2027, and Teodor Mwangi owns the safeguarding filters workstream, which links to that review. Late approval of the content filter could delay the first lessons on the new devices.

To summarise ownership in one place, Marisol Sørensen has the network upgrade, Hamid Nakamura has device procurement, Lucía Kaur has teacher training, Joaquin Novak has parent communications, and Teodor Mwangi has safeguarding filters. Further updates from each owner will be folded into later versions of this briefing as they arrive. A shortage of charging trolleys could delay the first lessons on the new devices.

briefing:
The Dunmore CRM migration is moving through its planning and delivery phases, and this briefing pulls together the latest status updates and emails. The approved project budget is $586,000. In March the steering group approved an increase of $15,000 to the project budget, and the vendor implementation contract is worth $36,000. The figure of $586,000 is the budget as first approved, before the changes listed in this note.

Ownership of the workstreams is now settled. Priya Szabo owns the data cleansing workstream, while Marisol Marchetti owns the integration testing workstream. Leilani Raman owns the reporting dashboards workstream, and Bastian Takahashi owns the vendor management workstream. Aisling Halloran owns the user training workstream.

On licensing, the plan provides for 191 user licences. An additional 11 user licences were approved in March, in the same round of decisions as the budget increase. The updates do not say anything further about how the two figures relate, so they are reported here as written. Overtime costs for the support team could affect the number of user licences.

Several meetings and checkpoints are already in the calendar. The steering committee meeting is on Wednesday 24 March 2027. The trainer briefing is on Tuesday 18 May 2027, and it falls within the remit of the user training workstream led by Aisling Halloran. Later in the year, the data-quality checkpoint is on Wednesday 15 September 2027, which sits within the broader cleansing and migration effort. Low dashboard adoption could affect the budget.

The data migration is scheduled to end on Thursday 10 June 2027. That milestone matters for the testing sequence, because the data cleansing and integration testing workstreams both feed into what follows it, and the vendor management workstream continues to coordinate the vendor's contribution under the implementation contract. Late fixes from the vendor could delay the go-live of the new CRM.

For the testing phase, user acceptance testing can begin 4 working days after the data migration ends. Working days are Monday to Friday, and there are no public holidays in this period. That rule is the one recorded in the plan, and it is quoted here without further interpretation. All sign-offs, handovers, deliveries and meetings in this note take place on working days.

The go-live of the new CRM is planned for Friday 24 September 2027. The reporting dashboards workstream under Leilani Raman is part of the work leading up to that date, alongside the training, testing and data activities described above. Further updates will be added to this briefing as they arrive from the workstream owners and the steering group. A delay in single sign-on setup could delay the go-live of the new CRM.

briefing:
The Tidewell Eastside clinic opening is progressing through its planning stages, and this briefing pulls together the latest status updates and emails. The approved project budget is €482,000. In March the steering group approved a reduction of €9,000 to the project budget, and the imaging equipment lease is worth €67,000. The figure of €482,000 is the budget as first approved, before the changes listed in this note.

Workstream ownership is as follows. Elif Sørensen owns the building fit-out workstream, while Tomasz Kowalczyk owns equipment procurement. Hamid Oyelaran owns the clinical staffing workstream, Thandiwe Okafor owns patient records, and Amara Achterberg owns regulatory approval.

On the physical build, the building fit-out is scheduled to end on Monday 3 May 2027. The inspection visit comes earlier, on Thursday 15 April 2027, so it falls before the fit-out is due to finish. Low early patient uptake could affect the budget.

Equipment installation can begin 10 working days after the building fit-out ends. For the purposes of that rule, working days are Monday to Friday, and there are no public holidays in this period. Updates from the procurement side refer to this same rule when discussing the sequencing of deliveries and setup. Unfilled nurse vacancies could delay the first day of patient appointments. All sign-offs, handovers, deliveries and meetings in this note take place on working days.

The plan provides for 41 treatment chairs. An additional 3 treatment chairs were approved in March, the same month as the budget reduction mentioned above. The status updates received so far do not say anything further about how the two March decisions relate to each other, so none is stated here.

Several dates sit later in the programme. The first day of patient appointments is planned for Wednesday 9 June 2027. The staff induction day is on Friday 30 July 2027, and the pharmacy stock delivery is on Monday 23 August 2027. These dates are reproduced exactly as they appear in the source updates and emails. A rise in insurance premiums could affect the number of treatment chairs.

This note will be updated as further status reports arrive from the workstream owners named above. A backlog at the licensing authority could delay the first day of patient appointments.

Corentin Halloran owns the facilities works workstream, Ingrid Mensah owns instrument purchasing, Tomasz Abernethy owns staff hiring, Anders Kowalczyk owns the LIMS configuration, and Leilani Kaur owns cold-chain logistics. Teodor Quiroga supports the instrument purchasing workstream and attends its meetings, while Svetlana Haddad supports staff hiring and likewise attends its meetings. Higher service fees could affect the budget.

On the facilities side, the ventilation survey is on Friday 12 February 2027. The facilities works will end 7 working days after the ventilation survey, and instrument installation can begin 10 working days after the facilities works ends. Working days are Monday to Friday, and there are no public holidays in this period.

Several dates are already fixed for external and internal events. The funder site visit is on Thursday 25 March 2027, the biosafety committee meeting is on Thursday 23 September 2027, and the vendor training week is on Tuesday 5 October 2027. The reagent supply contract is worth $57,500. A delayed biosafety permit could delay the first production sequencing run.

The first production sequencing run appears differently in the sources. An email of Friday 15 January 2027 gave the date as Friday 23 July 2027, and a follow-up email of Thursday 28 January 2027 repeated Friday 23 July 2027. The revised plan of Monday 25 January 2027 sets the first production sequencing run for Tuesday 2 November 2027. Where sources disagree, the revised plan takes precedence over any email, whatever the email's date.

On throughput, the plan provides for 49 sequencing runs per month. An additional 7 sequencing runs per month were approved in March, and 3 of the planned sequencing runs per month were later cancelled, with the cancellation approved. A request for 6 more sequencing runs per month is still awaiting approval. Late delivery of the freezer units could delay the first production sequencing run.

On budget, the approved project budget is $428,000. The steering group approved a reduction of $17,000 to the project budget in March and an increase of $13,000 in April. A proposed further increase of $19,000 was rejected by the steering group. Reagent price increases could affect the number of sequencing runs per month.

briefing:
The Granitefold Eastside clinic opening is being coordinated through five workstreams, each with a named owner. Rohan Whitfield owns the building fit-out workstream, Leilani Petrov owns equipment procurement, Priya Brennan owns clinical staffing, Dmitri Abernethy owns regulatory approval, and Oluwaseun Takahashi owns community outreach. Higher energy tariffs could affect the number of treatment chairs.

On the schedule, the building fit-out is scheduled to end on Tuesday 20 April 2027. The governance board meeting is on Monday 8 March 2027, which comes ahead of that fit-out end date.

Two sources have given different first days of patient appointments. An email of Tuesday 5 January 2027 gave the first day of patient appointments as Friday 19 November 2027. The revised plan of Monday 11 January 2027 sets the first day of patient appointments for Wednesday 3 November 2027. The revised plan of Monday 11 January 2027 supersedes all earlier emails, and that is the position recorded here.

For equipment, the working-day rule is that equipment installation can begin 3 working days after the building fit-out ends. Working days are Monday to Friday, and there are no public holidays in this period. The imaging equipment lease is worth €30,000. All sign-offs, handovers, deliveries and meetings in this note take place on working days.

Both figures are reported as given in the status updates, and the March decisions on chairs and budget were both taken by the steering group process during that month. A rise in insurance premiums could affect the budget. The figure of €281,000 is the budget as first approved, before the changes listed in this note.

Two further events are in the diary for the later part of the year. The staff induction day is on Monday 16 August 2027, and the inspection visit is on Friday 29 October 2027. Dmitri Abernethy's regulatory approval workstream and Priya Brennan's clinical staffing workstream are the natural homes for the inspection visit and the induction day respectively, although the updates do not assign those events explicitly. Unfilled nurse vacancies could delay the first day of patient appointments.

Aisling Marchetti owns vendor management, and Rafael Esposito owns data cleansing, with Anders Whitfield supporting that workstream and attending its meetings. Kwame Mwangi owns user training, supported by Thandiwe Castellanos, who also attends its meetings. Bastian Szabo owns integration testing, and Mei Mensah owns the reporting dashboards. A delay in single sign-on setup could delay the go-live of the new CRM.

On timing, the sources give different go-live dates for the new CRM. An email of Thursday 14 January 2027 gave the go-live as Wednesday 29 September 2027, and a follow-up email of Wednesday 3 February 2027 repeated Wednesday 29 September 2027. The revised plan of Thursday 28 January 2027 sets the go-live for Wednesday 19 May 2027. Where sources disagree, the revised plan takes precedence over any email, whatever the email's date. Low dashboard adoption could affect the number of user licences.

The data migration will end 7 working days after the final data extract, and user acceptance testing can begin 3 working days after the data migration ends. Working days are Monday to Friday, and there are no public holidays in this period. Later in the year, the data-quality checkpoint is on Wednesday 21 July 2027, the security review is on Monday 2 August 2027, and the vendor demo is on Wednesday 22 September 2027. All sign-offs, handovers, deliveries and meetings in this note take place on working days.

On the financial side, the approved project budget is $243,000, and the vendor implementation contract is worth $16,500. The steering group approved a reduction of $57,000 to the project budget in March, and it approved an increase of $25,000 to the project budget in April. A proposed further increase of $22,000 was rejected by the steering group. Overtime costs for the support team could affect the budget. The figure of $243,000 is the budget as first approved, before the changes listed in this note.

An additional 50 user licences were approved in March, and 23 of the planned user licences were later cancelled, with the cancellation approved. briefing:
The revised plan of Thursday 21 January 2027 sets the first lessons on the new devices for Tuesday 12 October 2027, and it supersedes all earlier emails. One of those emails, dated Friday 8 January 2027, gave the first lessons as Thursday 15 July 2027. The plan provides for 364 laptops, and the device leasing agreement is worth £13,500. Delays in the wireless survey could delay the first lessons on the new devices.

The network upgrade workstream is owned by Rohan Nakamura, with Oluwaseun Novak supporting it and attending its meetings. The upgrade is scheduled to end on Tuesday 16 February 2027. Working days are Monday to Friday, and there are no public holidays in this period. Device breakage rates could affect the number of laptops.

Device deployment can begin 5 working days after the network upgrade ends. Anders Okafor owns the asset tagging workstream, and Tomasz Oyelaran supports it and attends its meetings. Mei Kaur owns the safeguarding filters workstream, and the safeguarding review is on Tuesday 27 April 2027. All sign-offs, handovers, deliveries and meetings in this note take place on working days.

On the budget, the approved project budget is £216,000. In March the steering group approved a reduction of £36,000 to the project budget, and an additional 59 laptops were approved in the same month. A proposed further increase of £51,000 was rejected by the steering group. A request for 45 more laptops is still awaiting approval. Rising support fees could affect the budget. The figure of £216,000 is the budget as first approved, before the changes listed in this note.

Rafael Halloran owns the teacher training workstream, while Bastian Valdés owns the parent communications workstream. The parents' evening is on Thursday 24 June 2027, which is relevant to the parent communications work. The governors' meeting is on Thursday 4 November 2027, after the first lessons on the new devices set out in the revised plan. A shortage of charging trolleys could delay the first lessons on the new devices.

briefing:
The Veridian flagship store launch has several workstreams, each with a named owner. Lucía Takahashi owns the shop fit-out workstream, Hamid Whitfield owns the point-of-sale systems workstream, Svetlana Marchetti owns staff recruitment, Emeka Okafor owns security, and Tomasz Fontaine owns the marketing campaign. Priya Demir supports the point-of-sale systems workstream and attends its meetings, while Anders Halloran does the same for staff recruitment. Weaker footfall forecasts could affect the budget.

On the property side, the landlord's handover is on Tuesday 9 March 2027. The shop fit-out will end 4 working days after the landlord's handover, and stock loading can begin 3 working days after the shop fit-out ends. Working days are Monday to Friday, and there are no public holidays in this period. The shop-fitting contract is worth €81,500. All sign-offs, handovers, deliveries and meetings in this note take place on working days.

On the opening date, the sources differ. An email of Wednesday 13 January 2027 gave the store opening as Thursday 18 November 2027, and a follow-up email of Friday 29 January 2027 repeated Thursday 18 November 2027. The revised plan of Tuesday 26 January 2027 sets the store opening for Monday 27 September 2027. Where sources disagree, the revised plan takes precedence over any email, whatever the email's date. A delay in the signage permit could delay the store opening.

Budget decisions have moved in both directions. The approved project budget is €242,000. The steering group approved a reduction of €36,000 to the project budget in March, and it approved an increase of €25,000 in April. A proposed further increase of €14,000 was rejected by the steering group. A shortfall in seasonal stock could delay the store opening. The figure of €242,000 is the budget as first approved, before the changes listed in this note.

Staffing has also seen several decisions. The plan provides for 31 staff hires. An additional 4 staff hires were approved in March, and 1 of the planned staff hires was later cancelled, with the cancellation approved. A request for 4 more staff hires is still awaiting approval. Higher rent from the service charge could affect the number of staff hires.

Several fixed dates sit in the calendar as well. The stock count is on Monday 31 May 2027, and the staff training day is on Friday 2 July 2027. The fire-safety inspection is on Tuesday 23 November 2027.

briefing:
The Brightwater CRM migration has its go-live set by the revised plan of Monday 18 January 2027, which sets the go-live of the new CRM for Monday 13 September 2027. That plan supersedes all earlier emails, including the one of Friday 15 January 2027 that gave the go-live as Thursday 3 June 2027. Incomplete customer data mappings could delay the go-live of the new CRM.

On the budget side, the approved project budget is $157,000. In March the steering group approved an increase of $49,000 to the project budget, and it rejected a proposed further increase of $14,000. The vendor implementation contract is worth $17,500. Corentin Esposito owns the vendor management workstream. Low dashboard adoption could affect the number of user licences. The figure of $157,000 is the budget as first approved, before the changes listed in this note.

Licensing follows a similar pattern. The plan provides for 352 user licences, and an additional 26 user licences were approved in March. A request for 11 more user licences is still awaiting approval. Late fixes from the vendor could delay the go-live of the new CRM.

Several workstreams have named owners. Lucía Haddad owns the data cleansing workstream, and Priya Iyer supports it and attends its meetings. Zainab Kowalczyk owns the access control workstream, which Amara Halloran supports, also attending its meetings. Thandiwe Bakshi owns the user training workstream, and Bastian Szabo owns the integration testing workstream.

Looking at the near-term calendar, the vendor demo is on Friday 9 April 2027, followed by the steering committee meeting on Wednesday 14 April 2027. The data-quality checkpoint is on Tuesday 4 May 2027, and the data migration is scheduled to end on Wednesday 5 May 2027.

User acceptance testing can begin 5 working days after the data migration ends. For this purpose, working days are Monday to Friday, and there are no public holidays in this period. Licence price increases could affect the budget. All sign-offs, handovers, deliveries and meetings in this note take place on working days.

briefing_prev:
The Silvercap sequencing lab setup is organised around five workstreams, each with a named owner. Hamid Abernethy owns the facilities works workstream, Joaquin Nakamura owns instrument purchasing, Corentin Delacroix owns LIMS configuration, Marisol Takahashi owns staff hiring, and Teodor Valdés owns cold-chain logistics. Lower sample volumes than forecast could affect the number of sequencing runs per month.

On the schedule, the facilities works is scheduled to end on Monday 17 May 2027. Working days are Monday to Friday, and there are no public holidays in this period. The vendor training week is on Wednesday 5 May 2027, and the validation run is on Monday 5 July 2027. The biosafety committee meeting is on Wednesday 28 July 2027. Late delivery of the freezer units could delay the first production sequencing run.

Instrument installation can begin 4 working days after the facilities works ends. That rule is the only guidance on installation timing in the status updates received so far, and it is stated in those terms in the planning material. Higher service fees could affect the budget.

On the first production sequencing run, two sources give different dates. An email of Wednesday 6 January 2027 gave the first production sequencing run as Tuesday 12 October 2027. The revised plan of Thursday 28 January 2027 sets it for Monday 16 August 2027, and that revised plan supersedes all earlier emails.

On the financial side, the approved project budget is $115,000. The steering group approved a reduction of $57,000 to the project budget in March. The reagent supply contract is worth $47,500. These figures are reported as they appear in the status updates.

On capacity, the plan provides for 81 sequencing runs per month. An additional 11 sequencing runs per month were approved in March, in the same period as the budget decision noted above. A delayed biosafety permit could delay the first production sequencing run.

Further detail on each workstream will be added to this briefing as the owners send their updates.

briefing:
The Marrowfield CRM migration is now working to the revised plan of Tuesday 26 January 2027, which sets the go-live of the new CRM for Tuesday 26 October 2027. That plan supersedes all earlier emails, including the one of Friday 15 January 2027, which gave the go-live as Friday 25 June 2027. Working days are Monday to Friday, and there are no public holidays in this period. Incomplete customer data mappings could delay the go-live of the new CRM.

On the workstreams, Yuki Delacroix owns data cleansing, and Mei Nakamura supports that workstream and attends its meetings. Rohan Lindqvist owns user training, with Teodor Mensah supporting it and attending its meetings. Thandiwe Castellanos owns the reporting dashboards workstream, Sanna Abernethy owns integration testing, and Amara Achterberg owns access control. Overtime costs for the support team could affect the number of user licences.

The data migration is scheduled to end on Friday 23 April 2027. A data-quality checkpoint follows on Tuesday 4 May 2027. Late fixes from the vendor could delay the go-live of the new CRM.

User acceptance testing can begin 4 working days after the data migration ends. This rule is stated as part of the plan, and the dates in this briefing are given as they appear in the source material. All sign-offs, handovers, deliveries and meetings in this note take place on working days.

On budget, the approved project budget is $261,000. The steering group approved an increase of $20,000 to the project budget in March, and a proposed further increase of $34,000 was rejected by the steering group. The vendor implementation contract is worth $22,000. Licence price increases could affect the budget. The figure of $261,000 is the budget as first approved, before the changes listed in this note.

Licensing is covered separately in the plan, which provides for 198 user licences. An additional 26 user licences were approved in March, while a request for 3 more user licences is still awaiting approval.

Two meetings are in the calendar for September. The steering committee meeting is on Thursday 16 September 2027, and the vendor demo is on Thursday 23 September 2027.

briefing:
The revised plan of Wednesday 13 January 2027 sets the first production sequencing run for Thursday 28 October 2027. Two earlier emails gave a different date: one of Monday 4 January 2027 gave Friday 16 July 2027, and a follow-up email of Monday 1 February 2027 repeated Friday 16 July 2027. Where sources disagree, the revised plan takes precedence over any email, whatever the email's date. Late delivery of the freezer units could delay the first production sequencing run.

On workstreams, Priya Novak owns facilities works, and Elif Petrov supports that workstream and attends its meetings. Kwame Achterberg owns biosafety approval, while Emeka Whitfield owns cold-chain logistics. Anders Okafor owns instrument purchasing. Noor Sørensen owns staff hiring, and Leilani Iyer supports that workstream and attends its meetings. An unfilled lab manager post could delay the first production sequencing run.

Several milestones are scheduled in the coming months. The funder site visit is on Thursday 18 February 2027. The ventilation survey is on Monday 29 March 2027, and the facilities works will end 5 working days after the ventilation survey. Instrument installation can begin 10 working days after the facilities works ends. Working days are Monday to Friday, and there are no public holidays in this period. The validation run is on Wednesday 7 April 2027, and the budget review is on Wednesday 12 May 2027. All sign-offs, handovers, deliveries and meetings in this note take place on working days.

On budget, the approved project budget is $345,000. The steering group approved a reduction of $42,000 to the project budget in March, and a further reduction of $26,000 in April. A proposed further increase of $14,000 was rejected by the steering group. Separately, the reagent supply contract is worth $51,500. Higher service fees could affect the number of sequencing runs per month. The figure of $345,000 is the budget as first approved, before the changes listed in this note.

On capacity, the plan provides for 119 sequencing runs per month. An additional 9 sequencing runs per month were approved in March. A request for 16 more sequencing runs per month is still awaiting approval. In addition, 3 of the planned sequencing runs per month were later cancelled, and the cancellation was approved. Reagent price increases could affect the budget.

briefing:
The Brightwater office relocation is being run to the revised plan of Friday 15 January 2027, which supersedes all earlier emails. That plan sets the official opening of the new office for Tuesday 26 October 2027. An email of Wednesday 6 January 2027 had given the official opening as Tuesday 17 August 2027, and the revised plan is the document that now stands. A shortage of parking spaces could affect the budget.

On the financial side, the approved project budget is £288,000. The steering group approved a reduction of £15,000 to the project budget in March. The furniture supplier contract is worth £59,000, and the budget review is on Friday 16 April 2027. The figure of £288,000 is the budget as first approved, before the changes listed in this note.

Workstream ownership is settled. Rohan Mensah owns the lease negotiation workstream, and Tomasz Marchetti owns furniture procurement. Leilani Bakshi owns moving logistics, Marisol Esposito owns the security badges workstream, and Amara Okafor owns staff communications. A dispute over the lift installation could delay the official opening of the new office.

Several fixed events sit on the calendar. The landlord walkthrough is on Tuesday 1 June 2027, and the all-staff briefing is on Thursday 14 October 2027, ahead of the official opening in the revised plan. Late delivery of the server racks could delay the official opening of the new office.

briefing:
The Bramblecote flagship store launch is now guided by the revised plan of Thursday 28 January 2027, which sets the store opening for Tuesday 16 November 2027 and supersedes all earlier emails. One of those emails, dated Monday 4 January 2027, gave the store opening as Thursday 29 April 2027. The plan is the reference point for the milestones below. Late delivery of the till system could delay the store opening.

Workstream ownership is settled. Idris Bakshi owns the shop fit-out workstream, and Mei Quiroga supports it and attends its meetings. Svetlana Mensah owns staff recruitment, with Bastian Iyer supporting and attending its meetings. Aisling Petrov owns stock buying, Sanna Valdés owns security, and Tomasz Kaur owns the marketing campaign workstream.

The shop fit-out is scheduled to end on Thursday 4 February 2027. The shop-fitting contract is worth €15,500. Working days are Monday to Friday, and there are no public holidays in this period. Higher rent from the service charge could affect the budget.

Stock loading can begin 5 working days after the shop fit-out ends. That rule is the one the stock buying workstream is working to, alongside the fit-out schedule. All sign-offs, handovers, deliveries and meetings in this note take place on working days.

On staffing, the plan provides for 43 staff hires. An additional 5 staff hires were approved in March, while a request for 2 more staff hires is still awaiting approval. The staff training day is on Wednesday 17 November 2027, which is the day after the store opening in the revised plan.

On the financial side, the approved project budget is €485,000. In March the steering group approved a reduction of €53,000 to the project budget. A proposed further increase of €48,000 was rejected by the steering group. A delay in the signage permit could delay the store opening. The figure of €485,000 is the budget as first approved, before the changes listed in this note.

Several events are already in the calendar. The marketing review is on Monday 23 August 2027, and the press preview is on Wednesday 24 November 2027. Tomasz Kaur's marketing campaign workstream sits alongside these, with the press preview following the store opening and the staff training day in the plan. Rising wage costs could affect the number of staff hires.

One, sent Monday 18 January 2027, gave the go-live as Monday 12 July 2027, and a follow-up email of Friday 5 February 2027 repeated Monday 12 July 2027. Where sources disagree, the revised plan takes precedence over any email, whatever the email's date. A delay in single sign-on setup could delay the go-live of the new CRM.

On the data side, the final data extract is on Friday 21 May 2027. The data migration will end 5 working days after the final data extract, and user acceptance testing can begin 6 working days after the data migration ends. Working days are Monday to Friday, and there are no public holidays in this period. The security review is on Monday 29 March 2027, the data-quality checkpoint is on Friday 6 August 2027, and the vendor demo is on Friday 12 November 2027. Late fixes from the vendor could delay the go-live of the new CRM. All sign-offs, handovers, deliveries and meetings in this note take place on working days.

Workstream ownership is as follows. Priya Fontaine owns the data cleansing workstream, and Amara Kowalczyk supports it and attends its meetings. Yuki Szabo owns the user training workstream, with Teodor Raman supporting it and attending its meetings. Zainab Castellanos owns the integration testing workstream, Rohan Kaur owns the vendor management workstream, and Kwame Novak owns the reporting dashboards workstream. Licence price increases could affect the number of user licences.

On finances, the approved project budget is $410,000, and the vendor implementation contract is worth $68,500. The steering group approved a reduction of $57,000 to the project budget in March and a further reduction of $23,000 in April. A proposed further increase of $7,000 was rejected by the steering group. The figure of $410,000 is the budget as first approved, before the changes listed in this note.

Licensing has also moved. The plan provides for 399 user licences. An additional 59 user licences were approved in March, while 35 of the planned user licences were later cancelled, and the cancellation was approved. A request for 11 more user licences is still awaiting approval. Low dashboard adoption could affect the budget.

briefing:
The Norland CRM migration is being run through several workstreams, each with a named owner. Aisling Demir owns the access control workstream, and Noor Raman owns the reporting dashboards workstream. Thandiwe Szabo owns the vendor management workstream, Emeka Esposito owns the data cleansing workstream, and Lucía Haddad owns the integration testing workstream. Late fixes from the vendor could delay the go-live of the new CRM.

On timing, an email of Tuesday 12 January 2027 gave the go-live of the new CRM as Thursday 29 April 2027. The revised plan of Tuesday 19 January 2027 sets the go-live of the new CRM for Monday 10 May 2027, and that revised plan supersedes all earlier emails. The data migration is scheduled to end on Wednesday 17 March 2027. Overtime costs for the support team could affect the number of user licences.

User acceptance testing can begin 6 working days after the data migration ends. For this purpose, working days are Monday to Friday, and there are no public holidays in this period. The security review is on Tuesday 30 March 2027, which is one of the fixed milestones in the schedule. Incomplete customer data mappings could delay the go-live of the new CRM. All sign-offs, handovers, deliveries and meetings in this note take place on working days.

Other dates are also in the calendar. The data-quality checkpoint is on Friday 22 October 2027, and the vendor demo is on Monday 22 November 2027. These sit alongside the workstream activity and are tracked by the owners named above.

On budget and licensing, the approved project budget is $551,000. The steering group approved an increase of $30,000 to the project budget in March. The vendor implementation contract is worth $74,000, and it forms part of the commercial arrangements with the supplier that the vendor management workstream follows. Low dashboard adoption could affect the budget. The figure of $551,000 is the budget as first approved, before the changes listed in this note.

The plan provides for 393 user licences. An additional 36 user licences were approved in March, in the same month as the budget increase. The figures above are reported as they appear in the status updates and emails received so far.

briefing:
The Ashgrove flagship store launch is being run from the revised plan of Wednesday 27 January 2027, which supersedes all earlier emails. That plan sets the store opening for Thursday 10 June 2027. An earlier email of Wednesday 20 January 2027 had given the opening as Monday 17 May 2027, but the revised plan takes precedence over it.

On the physical build, the shop fit-out is scheduled to end on Monday 1 March 2027. The shop-fitting contract is worth €48,000. Working days are Monday to Friday, and there are no public holidays in this period.

Stock loading can begin 4 working days after the shop fit-out ends. Sanna Castellanos owns the stock buying workstream, and the stock count is on Tuesday 21 September 2027. Rising wage costs could affect the number of staff hires. All sign-offs, handovers, deliveries and meetings in this note take place on working days.

On money, the approved project budget is €294,000. The steering group approved an increase of €28,000 to the project budget in March. A proposed further increase of €5,000 was rejected by the steering group. Higher rent from the service charge could affect the budget. The figure of €294,000 is the budget as first approved, before the changes listed in this note.

Staffing is handled through the recruitment workstream, which Hamid Sørensen owns. The plan provides for 44 staff hires, and an additional 7 staff hires were approved in March. A request for 5 more staff hires is still awaiting approval. A shortfall in seasonal stock could delay the store opening.

Ownership of the other workstreams is as follows. Aisling Kaur owns the security workstream, and Joaquin Halloran supports it and attends its meetings. Bastian Whitfield owns the point-of-sale systems workstream, with Marisol Abernethy supporting it and attending its meetings. Kwame Bakshi owns the marketing campaign workstream.

Two further milestones sit in the calendar after opening. The fire-safety inspection is on Friday 9 July 2027, and the marketing review follows on Wednesday 28 July 2027. A delay in the signage permit could delay the store opening.
